text: From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued Enchantment day-use permit are required. In winter the road is usually gated well below the trailhead, adding miles on foot or ski.

From US 2 on the west side of Leavenworth, turn south on Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR 7601) and follow the washboarded, potholed road about 3.1 miles to the Eightmile Lake Trailhead, about 3,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

From US 2 on the west side of Leavenworth, turn south on Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FR 7601, signed for the Eightmile Trailhead. The trailhead is 3.1 miles up this washboarded, potholed road at about 3,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and the area is within the Enchantment permit area, so fill out the self-issued day-use permit.

Leave I-90 at Exit 80 and follow SR-903 north through Roslyn and Ronald and along Cle Elum Lake for about 14.8 miles to where the maintained road ends, then continue about 12.3 miles on the gravel Cle Elum Valley Road (FR 4330) and the short NF-153 spur to the Cathedral Rock trailhead for Trail #1345, at about 3,350 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is s

Drive the Cle Elum River Road (SR 903) to Salmon La Sac, then bear right just past the ranger station onto Forest Road 4330 - a rough road - and follow it about twelve miles to its end at roughly 3,350 feet. Two trailheads sit within a few yards of each other here, so it's easy to start wrong: the Hyas Lake and Deception Pass trail heads north, while the Cathedral Rock trail, #1345, heads west and

Drive up the Cle Elum River valley on Forest Service Road 4330 (Cle Elum Valley Road), about 13 miles past Salmon-la-Sac, to its end at the trailhead, roughly 3,400 feet. The access road is rough gravel and is best driven with a high-clearance or 4x4 vehicle.

From US 2 on the west side of Leavenworth, turn south on Icicle Road and drive 4.2 miles to the paved Snow Lakes Trailhead lot at about 1,300 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park. Day trips need the free self-issued Enchantment permit at the trailhead; overnight stays from May 15 to Oct 31 need a quota permit.
From Leavenworth, follow Icicle Road (Forest Road 7600) about 4.2 to 4.3 miles to the Snow Lakes Trailhead, at roughly 1,350 feet. Park in the lot on the south side of the road at the trailhead.

From Hoodsport, drive about 14 miles north on US 101 to the Hamma Hamma River Road (FR 25) and follow it roughly 6.5 miles to FR 2480. Take FR 2480 about 3 miles to FR 2401, then FR 2401 another 7 to 7.5 miles to where it crosses Jefferson Creek, in the Jefferson Lake trailhead area at about 2,440 feet. Park in the turnout just after the crossing — there is no formal trailhead sign, and no parking

pins.name: NF-110 gravel pull-off (Infinite Bliss / Southwest Ledges parking)

text: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE about 0.4 mile and turn right onto SE Middle Fork Road (FR 56). Drive about 12.3 miles to the fork just past the Taylor River bridge, keep right on the Middle Fork Road, and continue about 1 mile to a small gravel pullout with room for about five cars, at roughly 1,170 ft. Washouts on this road have at times added a mile or more of walking.

Drive to the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trailhead, the large lot at the end of FR 56, at about 1,040 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or the day-use fee is required to park. This is a long car-to-car day with about 5,200 ft of gain, so most parties are pulling out of the lot around 5 a.m. to keep daylight in hand.

pins.name: Garfield Ledges trailhead — NF-110 spur leaves here; park about 1/3 mile up the spur

text: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE about 0.4 mile and turn right onto SE Middle Fork Road (FR 56). Follow it about 12.2 miles to the Garfield Ledges trailhead, just across the Taylor River bridge at the fork with the Taylor River Road. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required.

From US 101 about 36 miles north of Hoquiam, one mile south of Amanda Park, turn east onto the Lake Quinault South Shore Road and follow it toward the head of the valley. The first 10 miles or so are paved and the rest is gravel, ending after roughly 20 miles at the Graves Creek Trailhead at 550 ft; allow about an hour for that final 20 miles. South Shore Road has been closed by a washout about 8

Drive to the road end at Graves Creek in the park's southwest corner. Overnight trips need a reserved wilderness permit — Enchanted Valley is a quota zone and the summer-season permits are released online months ahead of the season — and a bear canister is required in the valley. The trail leaves the lot heading east up the East Fork Quinault River.

pins.name: North Fork Quinault Trailhead / Ranger Station

text: Drive to the North Fork Quinault Ranger Station and trailhead at the end of North Fork Quinault River Road (North Shore Road), about 17 miles east of US-101 at Lake Quinault. It is a road-end trailhead at roughly 500 feet inside Olympic National Park, and an NPS entrance fee applies. No permits are issued at the trailhead: every overnight camp used on this route (Halfway House or Elip Creek, Low D

From US 101 at Amanda Park on Lake Quinault, turn east on North Shore Road and follow it about 17 miles, the upper part on gravel, to its end at the North Fork Ranger Station and trailhead. The park entrance fee applies; no Northwest Forest Pass is needed.

pins.name: North Fork Quinault Trailhead (North Shore Road)

text: From US 101 at the west end of Lake Quinault, near Amanda Park, turn east onto North Shore Road and follow it about 17 miles to its end at the North Fork Quinault trailhead and ranger station. A national park entrance pass is required, plus a wilderness permit for overnight stays.

pins.name: North Fork Quinault Trailhead (North Shore Road, road's end)

text: From US-101 at Lake Quinault, take North Shore Road about 14 miles to the North/South Shore intersection, then North Fork Quinault Road about 4 miles to the trailhead and ranger station; the last 4 miles are narrow gravel. An Olympic National Park wilderness camping permit is required.

From Hoodsport, drive about 14 miles north on US 101 and turn left at milepost 318 onto Hamma Hamma River Road (FR 25). Follow it about 12 miles, paved for the first 7.5 miles past the Lena Lake trailhead and gravel beyond, to the Putvin Trailhead pullout on the right at about 1,600 ft. No parking pass is required; camping at the lake needs a national park wilderness permit.

Park at the unmarked pullout on Hamma Hamma River Road (Forest Service Road 25), about 1,600 feet, roughly 4.5 miles past the Lena Lake trailhead. A slide near road mile 10.5 has at times closed the last 1.2 miles of the road; check current Forest Service status, since a closure would add a road walk to reach the pullout. The Putvin Trail itself (#813) is a steep, primitive path, unmaintained in i

From US 2 about 1.9 miles east of Skykomish, turn south on Foss River Road (FR 68); the pavement ends at 1.2 miles. Stay right at the Y at 3.5 miles, and at 4.7 miles, just before a bridge, turn left onto FR 6835 (the sign is easy to miss) and drive 1.9 miles to the West Fork Foss trailhead at about 1,600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park; self-issue the free wild

pins.name: FR 6835 roadside pullout past the East Fork Foss bridge

text: From US-2 at Skykomish, follow Foss River Road (FR 68) about 4.7 miles, turn left onto FR 6835, and continue about half a mile to the shoulder pullout just past the concrete bridge over the East Fork Foss River. There is no sign and no formal trailhead — parking is on the road shoulder — and a Northwest Forest Pass is required for the road.

The trailhead sits at the end of Forest Road 68, about 4.1 miles from US Highway 2 at Skykomish, at roughly 1,650 feet. A self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit and a Northwest Forest Pass are required at the trailhead kiosk.

pins.name: East Fork Foss River / Necklace Valley Trailhead

text: From US 2, about 0.5 mile east of the Skykomish Ranger Station, turn right (south) onto Foss River Road (FS Road 68) and drive 4.2 miles to the signed East Fork Foss River trailhead lot on the left, at about 1,650 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued wilderness permit are required.

From Quilcene, drive south on US-101 about 15 miles to the Duckabush Recreation Area, then turn west onto Duckabush River Road/Forest Service Road 2510 and follow it about 6 miles before continuing on FS Road 2510-060 to the road-end trailhead, at about 440 feet. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park and there is no potable water at the trailhead (the nearest is at Interrorem Cabin); you'll

Drive US 2 east past Skykomish about 12 miles to the sharp hairpin turn. Immediately after the Tunnel Creek bridge, turn right onto unsigned FS Road 6095 (only possible from the eastbound lane) and follow the narrow, potholed gravel road 1.2 miles, keeping left at two quick forks, to the trailhead at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit are

There is no drive to the trailhead proper — the Dosewallips River Road (FR-2610), off Hwy 101 near Brinnon, has been closed to vehicles at a washout since 2002, and the washout parking is where your car stops. From here it is roughly 6.5 miles of old roadbed up to the former ranger station and trailhead, which nearly every party bikes rather than walks; that stretch works out to about 13 miles ove

From US 101 at Brinnon, turn west onto Dosewallips Road (FR 2610) at milepost 306, just north of Dosewallips State Park, and drive about 8.5 miles to where the road is closed to vehicles at the washout; park along the roadside. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park.

From US-101 at Brinnon, turn onto Dosewallips Road and follow it inland about 8.5 miles to the road-end parking below the washout, which is as far as a car goes; the road has been shut to vehicles since the 2002 flood and remains so. Park here, and note that a mountain bike saves real time on the road miles beyond.
From US-101 at Brinnon, turn west onto the Dosewallips Road and drive about 8.5 miles to where it ends at the washout, and park along the road.

Drive US 2 to Stevens Pass and park in the large lot signed for the Pacific Crest Trail on the south side of the highway, just east of the ski area buildings, at about 4,060 ft. Fill out the free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit before starting.

pins.name: Stevens Pass North Lot / Skyline Lake-PCT Trailhead

text: Drive US 2 to Stevens Pass, about 65 miles east of Everett, and park in the large ski area lot on the north side of the highway. Walk to the small utility building near the east end of the lot, where the unsigned path begins. No parking pass is required.

From US-2 at Skykomish, turn north on Beckler River Road (FS-65). After about 0.8 mile turn left onto FS-6510, and in about a mile turn onto Eagle Creek Road (FS-6514). About five miles in, keep on spur 410 at the fork and continue past the Eagle Lake trailhead to the road's end, a small pullout at about 3,480 ft; the road gets rockier just before it ends. Roughly 6.5 miles of gravel and dirt from

Park at the Yodelin lot on US 2, the former Yodelin ski area's lot now used for overflow parking, around milepost 60 and about a mile east of the Stevens Pass summit at roughly 3,600 feet; it sits across the highway from the Yodelin community entrance. From the car you cross US 2 on foot and pick up the old ski-area access road, following it to its end before heading west up the Nason Creek valley

From Leavenworth, drive west on US-2 about 21.5 miles and turn left onto White Pine Road (FS Road 6950); follow it to the road end at the Whitepine Creek Trailhead, ignoring right-hand turns into private or gated land. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

pins.name: US-2 roadside pullout at WSDOT maintenance yard

text: Park at the unmarked shoulder pullout on US-2 by the WSDOT maintenance and tunnel-entrance yard, roughly 6 to 7 miles east of Stevens Pass. There is room for two or three cars and no permit is needed, but check for posted no-parking signs. Nothing here is signed — there is no trailhead, no trail number and no maintained tread anywhere on this route.

The trailhead is a small dirt pullout on the north side of US 2 near milepost 73, about 27 miles west of Leavenworth, at roughly 2,675 feet. Look for the signed Rock Mountain Trail #1587 and the powerlines the trail climbs under; it is an easy pullout to drive past. There is no fee or permit and no facilities of any kind. There is also no water at the trailhead and essentially none above the creek

From Skykomish take the Beckler River Road (FR 65) north, then follow the FR 6510 / FR 6514 / FR 6517 spur network — about 10.8 miles of gravel and dirt past the pavement — to the road end. The spurs can be rough or snow-blocked into early summer. There is no maintained trail beyond the pull-off and no water anywhere above the car, so carry all of it from here.

From US-2 near milepost 76, about 11.5 miles east of Stevens Pass or 24 miles west of Leavenworth, turn north onto the signed spur for Forest Road 657. The road is rough and high clearance is recommended; drive 1.5 miles to the Merritt Lake Trailhead at about 3,050 feet. No permit is required, but self-register at the trailhead kiosk before you start hiking.

From Stevens Pass, drive east on US-2 about 11.5 miles (from Leavenworth, about 23.5 miles west) and turn north onto Forest Road 657, a dirt road near milepost 76; take care turning across traffic. Follow it 1.5 miles to the Merritt Lake Trailhead at about 3,050 ft. The road is rough, so high clearance helps. No pass is required.
